Continue added phases in Kiln

See newly added phases on an existing feature, review the proposed work, and continue it once.

This release covers added phases on the same PRD. It excludes generating missing phases, undoing completed work and running a PRD roadmap. This snapshot uses local source documents. Source links open the published shared branch and may differ until these changes are landed.

For business review. Selected acceptance criteria and all 2 open assumptions. Implementation must use the full PRD and technical design. This is a dated snapshot; source links open the current documents.

01 / SECTION

Review what was added

A finished feature keeps its delivery history while Kiln checks the plan for additional work. The offer identifies the new phases, their order, the first phase and any readiness problem; discovery starts no implementation.

Key acceptance criteria & mockups

  • Count actual unfinished phase leaves. Numbering gaps, renamed documents, split parents and work completed elsewhere do not inflate the offer; assumption changes alone do not create a phase. AC-FIND-03
  • The check considers the shared checkout and current configured delivery base. Conflicting sources, missing evidence or an unreadable plan show a specific problem and a retry action; earlier counts and times are labelled as earlier results. AC-FIND-02, AC-FIND-04
  • A completed phase that was removed, reused, reopened or materially changed needs plan reconciliation. Kiln does not decide what earlier implementation to undo. AC-CONTINUE-03

What should work or look differently in this section?

Assumptions to confirm

CONTINUE-001Confidence: 85%Medium — someone leaving the finished page open may expect a new banner without reopening or clicking Check.Unanswered

Check on reopening and on request, without continuous monitoring?

Kiln automatically checks a completed feature when kiln run starts again or its page is opened/reloaded. A visible Check for new phases button checks while the page remains open. The first release does not promise continuous polling of an idle page or monitoring after Kiln exits.

Why this is proposed

The request asks what happens “if you start Kiln” after another session adds phases. Existing AC-KEEP-01 keeps Kiln in its terminal with no background service. Neither source settles continuous checking while a finished page remains open. Always polling is a plausible alternative, but is unnecessary for the stated restart workflow.

02 / SECTION

Continue with the right plan and permissions

A finished run waits for Continue. An unfinished run handed back from a manual session automatically picks up its revised plan once the current activity passes its completion checks.

Key acceptance criteria & mockups

  • Continue with N phases authorizes the displayed additional plan. Not now starts nothing and keeps a way to return. If the proposal or relevant prerequisites changed, Kiln refreshes it for a fresh choice without starting; repeated clicks and restarts cannot launch it twice. AC-OFFER-02, AC-OFFER-03
  • Earlier completed phases, sessions, delivery links and completion times stay in history. Added work uses a fresh conversation and does not rerun completed phases; work closed outside Kiln still needs applicable completion evidence. AC-CONTINUE-01
  • An integrated, verified prerequisite allows the next phase to start. When that phase explicitly includes preparation from an available source and existing authority permits it, Kiln performs and verifies the preparation before dependent implementation. Missing source, authority or a safe workspace blocks dependent work and shows the recovery action. AC-CONTINUE-02
  • Existing model settings, billing limits, pauses, workspace protection and repository permissions continue to apply. Continue grants no broader merge, production or spending authority, and new repositories pass the existing authorization checks. AC-CONTINUE-04
  • If planned preparation needs an uncovered delivery-base target, Authorize early merges separately shows the exact repository/branch and warns that existing CI/CD may run before the PRD finishes. This grant applies only to the proposed fresh run, changes no saved preference and starts no work. Continue remains separate. AC-CONTINUE-04
  • At manual handback, the active workspace is the plan source. Missing additions in another known source must be reconciled before advancement; Kiln never overwrites work to import them. Existing pauses and usage holds still apply, and editing the plan does not start work while the person controls the session. AC-HANDBACK-01–04
  • Additional work proceeds through the normal whole-PRD audits and delivery, including completion phases those audits add, without another continuation click. Earlier audit success or merged PRs cannot finish the revised scope; a new delivery is recorded alongside the earlier one. AC-CONTINUE-05

What should work or look differently in this section?

Assumptions to confirm

CONTINUE-002Confidence: 85%Medium — the person must first commit/integrate the changed requirements; a workflow that restarts a finished run directly from an unmerged requirements revision would need broader scope.Unanswered

Require a committed plan on the delivery base when restarting a finished run?

For a previously finished run, Kiln can discover saved local additions, but the revised document set must be committed together in the configured delivery base before Continue becomes available. Prerequisite work may already be integrated or be explicit, authorized preparation in the next phase. An unfinished run handed back from a manual session instead uses its active workspace and normal completion checks, and automatically continues through its updated plan.

Why this is proposed

The requested workflow begins after an earlier delivery. It does not decide whether a finished run should restart from uncommitted or unintegrated requirements. Requiring a settled requirements revision provides a reviewable starting point. This does not override documented, authorized preparation within a phase, as the fictional example illustrates. Example: In the fictional Comet Library plan, phases 9–15 are added work and phase 9 assigns integration of phase 8 from wt/catalog-accessibility. In the ready scenario, the revised plan is settled, the source is available and applicable authority is established. Continue with 7 phases starts that preparation inside Kiln; the person does not have to merge it first. This is an invented workflow example.
